subject: Post-call: PayFlux pricing & marketplace private offer mapping
messages:
From: Sarah Lang <sarah@payflux.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@payflux.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + pricing questions

Thanks for the call earlier, Aditya — quick recap from our side and a couple of follow-ups on pricing/marketplace mapping so we can move to procurement: 

- Estimated monthly token volume (production): ~1.2B tokens/month (we expect spiky inference traffic; ~70% generation, 30% embeddings/rerank).
- Target budget: rough upper bound $12k/mo.
- Target unit economics: we want to understand what a target $/1M tokens looks like for different deployment modes (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private via AWS Marketplace private offer).
- Marketplace question: our procurement team prefers to buy via AWS Marketplace private offer (PO). Can you map Redwood hosted MSRP to typical PO mapping (including marketplace commissions, AWS billing uplift, and any infra/partner fees) so we can see landed $/1M token to our P&L?

Next steps for us: procurement wants a worksheet showing per-1M token prices for each model tier, plus an example PO total for the 1.2B token volume. Can you send that by tomorrow? Also include any constraints around reserved capacity commitments required to hit the lower unit price.

Thanks,
Sarah Lang
Head of Platform, PayFlux

--
PayFlux Inc.
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lang <sarah@payflux.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + pricing questions

Great to chat, Sarah — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a first-pass pricing_workbook and a short SOW draft for procurement (see attachments). Below are the quick, pragmatic rules of thumb and a worked example so your procurement team has a model to work from immediately. I’ll follow up with a formal PO term sheet by EOD tomorrow.

Quick assumptions (please confirm):
- Monthly tokens: 1.2B (1,200M)
- Model mix: 70% gen (Llama-2-Chat-like), 30% embeddings/rerank (embedding-optimized model)
- Target: landed $/1M tokens to PayFlux via AWS Marketplace PO

Redwood internal MSRP (hosted API):
- Gen model: $6.00 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings: $2.00 / 1M tokens

Volume-weighted MSRP 
= 0.7 * $6 + 0.3 * $2 = $4.8 / 1M tokens

Marketplace mapping (example formula)
- Marketplace list uplift = 1.10 (10% marketplace seller fee baked into PO list)
- AWS billing uplift / taxes (example) = 1.03
- Reseller/partner margin (if applicable) = 1.05 (applied before marketplace fee)

Landed price per 1M via PO = MSRP * reseller_margin * marketplace_uplift * billing_uplift
Using conservative example (no reseller margin): $4.8 * 1.10 * 1.03 = $5.44 / 1M tokens

Total monthly cost (1.2B tokens) = 1,200 * $5.44 = $6,528 / month

If Redwood offers a reserved committed discount (Dedicated / reserved capacity) we can push MSRP down — for example a 30% committed discount on MSRP for gen tokens results in:
- Gen MSRP -> $4.20, embeddings -> $1.40 -> volume-weighted MSRP = $3.36
- PO landed = $3.36 * 1.10 * 1.03 = $3.80 / 1M => monthly = 1,200 * $3.80 = $4,560

Notes / caveats:
- Marketplace fees vary by contract and whether the buyer wants to include the marketplace invoice or have Redwood invoice directly; we can model both.
- Exact AWS PO line-item must include the PO ID and offer prices (we’ll draft).
- If PayFlux wants Redwood to absorb the 10% marketplace fee (possible in larger committed deals), that increases Redwood commit threshold; we can model it in the workbook.

Action items I’ll take:
- Attach pricing_workbook.xlsx with three scenarios (hosted MSRP, PO mapping, committed discount mapping).
- Draft short PO term sheet + SOW and push to DocuSign for procurement.

If you can confirm token split and whether you prefer Redwood to issue the invoice (direct) vs AWS Marketplace invoicing, we’ll finalize numbers.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx (pricing scenarios), PayFlux_SOW_draft.pdf
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + pricing questions

Adding a few technical/pricing clarifications from SE side: 
- Token assumptions: clarify whether your 1.2B tokens includes prompt+completions. If you expect long prompts (avg 1k tokens/request), effective token run-rate changes.
- Model selection: to hit the $/1M ranges above we recommend mixing a 8k context gen model for user-facing flows (70%) and an optimized 1k-context embeddings model for vectors (30%).
- Autoscale & burst: marketplace PO usually maps to hosted API SKU; for consistent bursts we recommend a small reserved baseline (e.g., Dedicated pool with burst to hosted). That allows predictable unit pricing under commit while still handling spikes.

I'll help populate the workbook with a sensitivity sheet (avg prompt length and % gen/embedding) — if Sarah confirms avg prompt length we can provide a tighter $/1M.

- Aisha Rahman
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya/Aisha — that worked example is super helpful. A few clarifications from procurement:

- Confirmed token split: 70% gen / 30% embeddings. Avg prompt+completion ~850 tokens.
- Target budget: we can stretch to $8k/mo if the PO landed price is <= $6.75 / 1M tokens.
- Procurement prefers the PO route; they will not accept Redwood direct-invoice for this purchase.
- Can Redwood provide an AWS Private Offer (we’ll need the PO ID and line-item pricing) and indicate whether Redwood can absorb the 10% marketplace fee in exchange for a 12-month commit?

Also looping Marta from AWS partners — can you confirm typical timeline for a Private Offer setup and any AWS-side uplift we should expect?

Thanks,
Sarah
